# Satish Upadhyaya

> Software Engineer II at Microsoft, working in the Azure Networking org.
> University of Colorado Boulder, B.S. Computer Science, 2021. Currently
> working with local LLMs and agentic development workflows.

## Usage

This content may be read, summarised, and cited with a link back to
https://satishupadhyaya.github.io/. It is not made available for inclusion in
model training corpora; see /robots.txt, which disallows training crawlers
while allowing search and answer engines.

## About

Satish Upadhyaya is a software engineer based in the United States. He
graduated from the University of Colorado Boulder with a B.S. in Computer
Science in Summer 2021 and works at Microsoft as a Software Engineer II in
the Azure Networking org.

At CU Boulder he was a Research Assistant in the SBS group, where he helped
build a scalable software system on the university's supercomputer cluster
for running large-scale building-energy simulations. A publication came out
of that lab on using meta-models in place of computationally intensive
simulations.

He interned at Microsoft on the Azure Networking team (remote, Summer 2020)
and at Workday on the Worksheets team (in person, 2019), and worked as a
course assistant for an introductory computer science course at CU Boulder.

Current interests: running local LLMs on his own hardware, and folding
agentic workflows into day-to-day software development. Outside of work he
is an avid hiker and skier.

Languages and tools: C#, Python, Home Assistant, computer vision libraries.

## Current work (private repositories, no public links)

- Agentic AI workflows for everyday software development, and running local
  large language models on self-hosted hardware.
- A home automation system built on Home Assistant covering lights, locks,
  and cameras, including a garage door that opens on license-plate
  recognition.

## Public projects

- [OpenPose Drone Control Via Body Movement](https://github.com/SatishUpadhyaya/Robotics-Final-Project):
  Drone control via MAVROS using keyboard input, ArUco tracking, and OpenPose.
- [Data Visualization Web App with Dash](https://github.com/SatishUpadhyaya/GWDataVisualizer):
  A tool for pulling analytics and statistics out of a dataset.
- [Project Euler](https://github.com/SatishUpadhyaya/ProjectEuler):
  Solutions to the first 49 Project Euler problems in Python 3.
- [NFL Home Field Predictor](https://github.com/SatishUpadhyaya/NFL_HomeFieldPredictor):
  An SVM-SVC model relating QB passer rating and final score to home/away
  advantage, built with pandas, NumPy, and scikit-learn.
